dataSources.name: Kemp, Herholdt, Whyte & Harrison 2001
dataSources.usedFor: Order-of-magnitude Kruger population thresholds. Kemp et al. (2001) estimated mature individuals capable of reproduction, snapped to a power of two. For a threshold T the range stored here is T/2 to 2T. Resident breeders use the lower neighbouring threshold; visiting breeders and non-breeding visitors use the upper neighbouring threshold. These figures are not a park census. Ambiguous taxonomy and species with no Kemp row have no number. Four later park surveys replace the Kemp range and keep it as a baseline. This site cites the numbers and does not host the PDF or the appendix.

dataSources.name: Birda SABAP2 Kruger checklist
dataSources.usedFor: Primary filter for families and species that regularly occur in Kruger. SABAP2 observation counts separate residents, regular migrants, and regular visitors from rare and accidental records. The checklist cites the GBIF occurrence download linked here.

dataSources.name: BirdLife South Africa Checklist of Birds in South Africa 2026
dataSources.usedFor: Official national list. Scientific names, English names, Afrikaans species names, and vagrant status come from this checklist.

dataSources.name: SANParks Kruger birds checklist
dataSources.usedFor: Park checklist, cited as 546 species. Used as context for which birds are treated as regular in Kruger. It did not supply the master species list.

dataSources.name: Avibase — Kruger National Park
dataSources.usedFor: Family-ordered checklist used as a cross-check. The default taxonomy there is Clements, with an IOC option. It informed borderline regular-versus-vagrant judgement and was not the master list.

dataSources.name: Wikipedia — List of birds of South Africa
dataSources.usedFor: Cross-check of family structure. The page is arranged on Clements and notes BirdLife South Africa status. The licence below is the licence of the Wikipedia text.

dataSources.name: Waterberg Bioquest — Voëls
dataSources.usedFor: Afrikaans family headings. Waterberg is outside Kruger. A heading was used only where a stable southern African family name could be verified. Species Afrikaans names were not taken from this page.

taxonomy.summary: Scientific names, English names, and family placement follow the IOC World Bird List as adopted by the BirdLife South Africa Checklist of Birds in South Africa 2026. Afrikaans species names come from that checklist. Afrikaans family headings come from Waterberg Bioquest only where a stable heading could be verified, and are left blank otherwise.
